events.continuity_hook: Adds a final operating check to the Idaho plant visit after the flights, hotel, and rental car were booked.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the drive timings, hotel arrival note, plant entry plan, rental-car fueling, and return-day buffer without reopening the core reservations.
events.scenario_brief: The Twin Falls plant sends a revised gate map, PPE pickup note, and a warning that harvest traffic may slow the Boise-to-Twin Falls drive. Jonah keeps the booked Monday afternoon one-stop to Boise, compact SUV, and Twin Falls hotel, but wants the late-arrival hotel check-in note, Tuesday 6:15 a.m. plant departure time, Wednesday debrief-to-airport drive buffer, and fuel and parking plan tightened. The only open item is whether to leave Twin Falls immediately after the debrief or build in a brief dinner stop before the evening flight.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a conference-planning episode after the Idaho food-plant trip is wrapped and his fall schedule fills back in.
events.interaction_goal: Build a flight and hotel shortlist around booth setup, panel timing, return flexibility, hotel quality, and downtown dinner logistics.
events.scenario_brief: A regional water-technology conference in Nashville adds Jonah to a partner-panel slot and asks him to be onsite for Monday morning booth setup. He needs a Sunday Bay Area departure that arrives early enough for convention-center check-in and slide review, plus a return after Wednesday afternoon sessions unless a vendor dinner extends him to Thursday. Hotel comparison should include the official convention hotel against a nearby higher-rated downtown property with easier meals; unresolved items are whether his teammate covers Wednesday teardown and whether the company rate beats the block.

events.continuity_hook: Refines the Nashville conference plan once the panel time, booth freight timing, and hotel block quality are clearer.
events.interaction_goal: Narrow the outbound flight, hotel selection, return window, and teardown-dependent schedule before committing.
events.scenario_brief: The panel time moves earlier to Monday 8:30 a.m., the booth crate arrival is confirmed for Sunday evening, and the official hotel block shows mixed guest feedback. Jonah wants to narrow between a Sunday afternoon nonstop on a non-United carrier and a United one-stop that lands later but earns loyalty credit; hotel choices are the connected convention hotel versus a better-rated property two blocks away with a small fridge and nearby restaurants. Still unresolved is whether Wednesday teardown is his job or can be handed off.

events.continuity_hook: Finalizes the Nashville conference travel once teardown responsibility and the hotel rate settle.
events.interaction_goal: Book the flights and hotel, add room and seat notes, and summarize the conference arrival and return timing.
events.scenario_brief: His teammate takes Wednesday teardown and the company rate at the nearby downtown hotel comes in within budget. Jonah books the Sunday afternoon nonstop because it protects the Monday panel and booth setup better than the later one-stop, reserves the higher-rated downtown hotel with a quiet-room note plus coffee maker and mini-fridge request, and sets the return for Wednesday evening after the last panel. Seats are selected with a window where available, and the conference agenda is trimmed to the required booth, panel, and client-meal commitments.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new municipal commissioning trip after the conference travel is set.
events.interaction_goal: Create a flight, rental-car, and hotel shortlist that protects the early gate entry while keeping Thursday return options realistic.
events.scenario_brief: A central Pennsylvania utility asks Jonah to review a membrane startup before the contractor turns the system over, with a Wednesday 7:00 a.m. gate entry and a possible Thursday noon procurement meeting. He needs Tuesday Bay Area-to-Harrisburg options compared with a Philadelphia nonstop plus the longer drive, including rental-car pickup time and enough evening prep at the hotel. Hotel options should favor a well-rated property near the plant with parking and workable restaurant access over an airport hotel; open items are whether the calibration kit arrives Tuesday and whether the procurement meeting stays on the calendar.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the central Pennsylvania utility trip from comparison to booking once the kit arrival and Thursday meeting timing are confirmed.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the flights, rental car, hotel reservation, room details, seat choices, and the two-day site agenda.
events.scenario_brief: The calibration kit is confirmed on the contractor truck, and procurement keeps the Thursday meeting but caps it at 11:30 a.m. Jonah books the Tuesday afternoon one-stop into Harrisburg because the shorter morning drive outweighs the Philadelphia nonstop, adds a compact SUV, and chooses the suburban hotel closest to the plant with strong guest feedback, parking, coffee maker, mini-fridge, and dinner options nearby. The return is set for Thursday late afternoon with one comfortable connection and window seats where available; the only remaining check is whether the utility needs visitor paperwork submitted the night before.
